structured_stats.description:
The '''Demoman''' is a starter splash damage tower that can be bought in the store for {{Coins|200}}. While targeting a specific enemy, it will also affect those around the target, dealing splash damage. 

At Levels 0-2, the '''Demoman''' takes one second to aim at an enemy before throwing its explosive grenades. This only affects the damage for the first throw, as it means the '''Demoman''' has to wait a second before throwing it. While it is aiming, it will focus on one enemy until it throws its explosive grenade, after which it can target a different one. If the targeted enemy dies, the '''Demoman''' will continue targeting it, though its grenade will not land where it died, it will throw it further away, which is generally the area where the enemy would have travelled to if it did not die. The '''Demoman''' will also continue to aim at that enemy even if it leaves its range, allowing it to attack outside of its range. After the first throw, while the '''Demoman''' still aims, this does not affect its firerate. The explosion caused by the '''Demoman''' does not have damage drop-off. The '''Demoman''' can also damage [[Lead (Attribute)|Lead]] enemies.

The '''Demoman''' is great for large hordes of non-boss enemies, except for those immune to splash damage. It is relatively weak against major bosses, though it can be useful in tackling the enemies that spawn from some major bosses. The '''Demoman''' is considered an early game to mid-game tower, though in late game it can be quite useful for swarm-clearing when multiple are placed down.

Some inherited from spawner enemy }} ==Description== The '''Corpse''' is an enemy that only appears when spawned through the [[Corpse (Attribute)|Corpse]] attribute. Uniquely, its statistics are actually heavily based on the enemy that summoned it, instead of having its own statistics, though it does have some statistics that do not change. This is because the '''Corpse''' is not its own enemy, it is actually the enemy it spawned from with a changed display name and altered statistics. Most notably, it has 100% defense, and it has the [[Corpse (Attribute)|Corpse]], [[Stun Immunity]] and [[Burn Immunity]] attributes. Its health is 75% of the enemy that it spawned from. Additionally, some of the attributes the enemy it spawned from are also inherited. The only exception to this is [[Hidden (Attribute)|Hidden]], which is removed upon the enemy's death. ==Appearance== The '''Corpse''' does not have a consistent appearance, as the model it uses is based on the enemy it spawned from, though it does have certain characteristics which are consistent between them all. The '''Corpse''' is the body of the enemy it spawned from made entirely out of black molten rocks. Any images present on the enemy, such as faces, will remain on them even as a '''Corpse'''. ==Strategy== *The '''Corpse''' is not a threatening enemy, as it cannot move to the entrance, meaning losing to it is impossible. Its main purpose is to act as a shield for enemies behind it. **However, it can be relatively an inconvenience with its 100% defense and tendency to distract towers from attacking actual enemies. **Towers like the [[Electroshocker]] or [[Toxic Gunner]] can be used to drop its defense, as it is very high. The [[Pyromancer]] cannot be used since it has [[Burn Immunity]]. **Towers like the [[Ranger]] or [[Mortar]] can be used to take care of any corpses that are too far away from your main defenses with their high range. *The '''Corpse''' is required to be killed before a match can end. **Waves can be skipped while only '''Corpses''' are on the path, as that still grants the wave clear bonus. Additionally, infinite waves cannot be skipped at all. ***If you have the [[DJ Booth]], you can exploit this by repeatedly using its ''Drop The Beat'' ability on Green track to make as much cash as you want. *As the '''Corpse''' is technically not a unique, summoned enemy, but instead the slightly altered version of the enemy it spawned from, the [[Cowboy]] is able to generate cash from it. ==Gallery== {{Gallery| {{GalleryHeader|Previous Variants}} MoltenCorpseMolten.png|First version (11 December 2024 – 12 March 2025) {{GalleryHeade

==Description==
'''Defense''' is a status value given to certain enemies and units. Enemies may spawn with this naturally, or be granted this through a litany of means.

==Mechanics==
There are two types of defense statistic. The main defense statistic is ''Percentage Defense'' which is used to calculate ''Effective Damage''.

''Percentage Defense'' is the actual defense percentage you see on an enemy or unit. However, this does not mean that if an enemy has 50% defense damage dealt towards it will be decreased 50%. In reality, the number listed is far closer to the percentage of additional health that '''Defense''' gives it.

''Effective Damage'' is the actual damage dealt towards an enemy by a tower once ''Percentage Defense'' is applied. ''Effective Damage'' is calculated by calculating

::<big>'''Original Damage ÷ (1 + Percentage Defense)'''</big>

where ''Percentage Defense'' is changed from a percentage into its equivalent decimal number (for instance, 50% would be 0.5 in decimal form). For example, a tower that deals 100 damage attacking an enemy with 50% defense would deal 67 damage as 100 ÷ (1 + 0.5) = 66.67 to two decimal places. Due to ''Effective Damage'' always being rounded up to the nearest integer, 66.67 rounds up to 67. Prior to the [[v1.1.0|Entity System Update]], ''Effective Damage'' was always rounded down to the nearest integer.

Unit defense works identically to enemy defense, reducing damage from enemy abilities and collision.

===Countering Defense===
'''Defense''' can reduce the damage output of most towers significantly.

There are a couple of towers and consumables that can melt the ''Percentage Defense'' value of enemies, allowing your towers to deal more damage. A few certain towers can also ignore defense. There are two types of defense melting towers. The first has them decrease ''Total Defense'' by a certain percentage. However, if the [[Pyromancer]], which melts defense by 50%, is decreasing defense of [[Fallen Hero]], which has 50% defense, this does not mean its defense will be lowered to 0%. Instead, it is decreased by 25% defense, as which is 50% of 50% defense. The defense removal can stack, so the [[Pyromancer]] and [[Electroshocker]] can together remove 70% ''Percentage Defense'', but two [[Pyromancer]]s cannot remove 100% ''Percentage Defense''. Instead, only 50% ''Percentage Defense'' can be melted. Additionally, defense melting from burn cannot stack with other burn towers, freeze defense melting cannot stack with other freeze towers and poison defense melting cannot stack with other poison towers.

The second type has them decrease ''Total Defense'' by a flat amount. For example, the [[DJ Booth]] at maximum power can melt 25% defense. This means that when melting defense of the [[Fallen Giant]], it will will melt its defense from 60% to 35%.

Both forms of defense melting do not interfere with each other and can stack. For example, if the [[DJ Booth]] decreases the [[Vindicator (Legacy)|Vindicator]]'s defense from 100% to 75%, the [[Pyromancer]] will reduce it from 75% to 25%, which is the same decrease (50% less defense) as if [[DJ Booth]] did not affect it. Likewise, if the [[Pyromancer]] decreases the [[Vindicator (Legacy)|Vindicator]]'s defense from 100% to 50%, the [[DJ Booth]] will still be able to decrease it by 25%, from 50% to 25%.

{{Removed|date = 6th of June 2026}}
{{Improve|this page and majority of tower/unit pages require updating}}
The '''Firerate Bug''', also known as the '''RoF (Rate of Fire) Bug''', was a bug that slightly increased the firerate of all towers and units. This increase was not displayed on the statistics in the game. This bug significantly affected the statistics of fast-firing towers, such as the [[Minigunner]] and [[Ace Pilot]], by significantly decreasing their DPS, whereas slow-firing towers like the [[Ranger]] or [[Sniper]] were hardly affected.

This has been fixed as of the 6th of June 2026, and all firerate statistics in the game are considered to be accurate unless affected by a different unrelated bug.

{{RightTOC}}

==Prior to 5th of June 2026==
The '''Firerate Bug''' affects all towers and units that can directly attack enemies, meaning the only towers that are not affected are the [[Farm]], [[Medic]] and the [[Firework Technician]] and the only units that are not affected are the [[Humvee]], [[Humvee 2]], [[Elf]], [[Bomber Elf (Unit)|Bomber Elf]], [[Skeleton (Unit)|Skeleton]], [[Giant Skeleton (Unit)|Giant Skeleton]] and [[Hallow Guard (Unit)|Hallow Guard]]. The '''Firerate Bug''' does not affect the firerate of some secondary attacks towers or units may perform, some damage-over-time effects applied by towers (like burn from the [[Pyromancer]]) or certain other cooldowns.

The '''Firerate Bug''' increases the firerate of a tower/unit depending on its firerate, which can vary anywhere between 0.017 and 0.032 seconds. The firerate increase affects fast firing towers the most; for example, the [[Minigunner]] at Level 4 should have a firerate of 0.09, but because of the '''Firerate Bug''', it has a firerate of about 0.117, decreasing its DPS from 166.67 to 128.20, which is a decrease of 38.47 DPS, or a loss of about 23.08 DPS. Meanwhile, slow firing towers are barely affected by it; for example, the [[Ranger]] at Level 4 should have a firerate of 8, but because of the '''Firerate Bug''', it has a firerate of about 8.025, decreasing its DPS from 156.26 to 155.76, which is a decrease of 0.30 DPS, or a loss of 0.2% DPS.

The [[Firerate Buff]] is also affected by the '''Firerate Bug''', making it less effective. For example, the Level 4 [[Minigunner]] without the '''Firerate Bug''' with a 50% firerate boost should have a firerate of 0.06, but with the '''Firerate Bug''' it has a firerate of 0.083. This means that its DPS with a 50% firerate boost is decreased from 250 to 180.72, which is a decrease of 69.28 DPS, or a loss of 27.71% DPS.

On this Wiki, the firerate statistic of all towers and units is increased by specific values based on the firerate. While technically possible to calculate by hand, due to the effort it would take, it is overall recommended to either use [[Help:Neowtext#ROFBUG|Neowtext]] or [https://fiheron.github.io/dps-calc/ an online calculator].

==Prior to the 9th of January 2023==
Prior to the 9th of January 2023, the firerate increase caused by the '''Firerate Bug''' for units was higher than it currently is. The firerate increase was generally around 0.03 seconds. For towers, the firerate increase remained at around 0.008 seconds.

On this Wiki, the firerate statistic of all towers and units after the [[V1.6.0|Violent Night Update]] and before the 9th of January 2023 is increased by 0.008 and 0.03 respectively, unless stated otherwise. This does not, however, mean the actual value is this; it can vary between towers and even between matches.

==Prior to the Violent Night Update==
Prior to the [[V1.6.0|Violent Night Update]], the firerate increase caused by the '''Firerate Bug''' for units was lower than it was before the [[V1.6.0|Violent Night Update]]. The firerate increases could be anywhere between 0.008 and 0.017 seconds, but the increase was generally around 0.008 seconds. This is the same as the current situation.

Build up chill to slow and freeze enemies in their tracks!|Store Description}} |-|Version 3 = {{QuoteBox|Chill enemies to a slow freeze!|Store Description}} |-|Version 2 = {{QuoteBox|Shoot an ice beam, freezing targets for a few seconds.|Store Description}} |-|Version 1 = {{QuoteBox|Freeze zombies temporarily with a freeze ray!|Former Store Description}} }} __TOC__ ==Description== The '''Freezer''' is a ground [[Towers|tower]] that fires an ice beam and applies chill and slow down enemies, freezing at later levels. It can be bought in the store for {{Coins|650}}. The '''Freezer''' targets a single enemy and fires a ''Frost Ray'', chilling the enemy and slowing it down. The chillness slowness effect stacks with each hit multiple times. This chillness effect also deals damage over time, chipping away the health of enemies affected by it. Starting from Level 2, it can freeze enemies. When the chillness slowness effect is higher than the max slowdown, the enemy will be frozen, which generally when targeting a single enemy takes four or five shots. Larger enemies will be frozen for a shorter amount of time than average sized enemies. Enemies with [[Freeze Immunity]] also cannot be frozen, slowed down or have their defense dropped by the '''Freezer'''. At Level 3+, the '''Freezer''' fires in bursts, with a short delay between them. Additionally, at Level 3+, it drops defense by 10% every tick. It can only decrease an enemy's defense by 33%. For example, if an enemy has 50% defense, it will be decreased by 16%. On top of this, it will also start dealing damage over time with its chill at Level 3. Additionally at Level 4, the '''Freezer''' gains the ability to throw a '''Frost Grenade''', freezing enemies within an explosion radius. The '''Freezer''' does well as an all-rounder support tower. Due to its generally low price and decent DPS, the '''Freezer''' can be a solid choice for early-game defense to mid game with very good cost efficiency. Towards late game, the '''Freezer''' is useful for stalling, defense melting and deal additional DPS through its damage over time, though its DPS is insufficient to deal with late-game waves alone. The '''Freezer''' has [[Lead (Attribute)|lead]] detection from Level 0 and [[Hidden (Attribute)|hidden]] detection from level 2. {{SameName|Lead|[[Lead (Attribute)|Attribute]] • [[Lead (Legacy Enemy)|Legacy Enemy]] • [[Lead|Modern Enemy]]}} {{For|the [[Lead Boss]]|[[Lead Balloon]]}} {{AttributeInfobox |title1 = Lead |image1 = LeadIcon.png |type = Enemy Type |detection = Lead Detection |immunities = Damage |sandbox = Yes |tag = {{AttrTag|Second|LeadIcon.png|Lead}} }} ==Description== '''Lead''' is an enemy type that prevents the enemy from being damaged by any tower that does not have lead detection. ==Mechanics== '''Lead''' enemies cannot be damaged by any tower without lead detection, though despite what the detection name suggests, they can still be targeted by towers without it unless other attributes prevent the tower from doing so. Only towers with lead detection can damage them. By default, [[Splash Damage]] (except [[Paintballer]]), fire damage and collision damage all have lead detection. Some towers cannot damage lead enemies with all their attacks as only some of them have it, such as the [[Archer]] not being able to damage ''Lead'' enemies with its arrows, but still being able to damage them through its burn.
